First, from the equation of the plane we get that the normal vector of $Π$ is $n=⟨5,0,2⟩.$

Now, we solve the Cartesian equation of $Π$ for $z$:

$$
\begin{aligned}5x+2z-8 & =0 \\ z & =-\frac{5}{2}x+4\end{aligned}
$$

If we put, say, $x=0,$ we get $z=4.$ Hence, the point $P(0,0,4)$ lies on $Π.$ Note that the position vector of $P$ is $p=⟨0,0,4⟩.$

Finally, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ (r-⟨0,0,4⟩)\cdot ⟨5,0,2⟩ & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
